original.text: But if A, in illustration (c), not dishonestly but in good faith, believing that it will be more for Z’s advantage to hold shares in the Bank of Bengal, disobeys Z’s directions, and buys shares in the Bank of Bengal, for Z, instead of buying Company’s paper, here, though Z should suffer loss, and should be entitled to bring a civil action against A, on account of that loss, yet A, not having acted dishonestly, has not committed criminal breach of trust.
original.derived_context:
Act: Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023
Chapter 17: OF OFFENCES AGAINST PROPERTY
Section 316: Criminal breach of trust.
Whoever, being in any manner entrusted with property, or with any dominion over property, dishonestly misappropriates or converts to his own use that property, or dishonestly uses or disposes of that property in violation of any direction of law prescribing the mode in which such trust is to be discharged, or of any legal contract, express or implied, which he has made touching the discharge of such trust, or wilfully suffers any other person so to do, commits criminal breach of trust.
But if A, in illustration (c), not dishonestly but in good faith, believing that it will be more for Z’s advantage to hold shares in the Bank of Bengal, disobeys Z’s directions, and buys shares in the Bank of Bengal, for Z, instead of buying Company’s paper, here, though Z should suffer loss, and should be entitled to bring a civil action against A, on account of that loss, yet A, not having acted dishonestly, has not committed criminal breach of trust.

phase11.final_answer: Good faith under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita means actions or beliefs conducted with due care and attention, and communications made in good faith for the benefit of others are not considered offences even if they cause harm.
phase11.summary_answer: Under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 'good faith' refers to actions or beliefs that are conducted with due care and attention.
phase11.detailed_answer: 'Good faith' is defined in Section 2(11) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, as actions or beliefs that are not considered to be in 'good faith' if they are done or believed without due care and attention. Additionally, Section 31 states that no communication made in good faith is an offence if it is made for the benefit of the person to whom it is directed, even if it causes harm. This indicates that good faith involves a consideration of the intent and the benefit to others, as illustrated in Section 27, where an action taken in good faith for a child's benefit, despite potential harm, is within the exception as long as the intent is not to cause harm.
